title: Gloop Goes to Monster School
text:
Fuzzyville Monster School report card for Gloop, age seven. Reading: Gloop reads very {adverb}. His favorite book is about a little monster who is afraid of {plural noun}. He has read it {number} times.

Math: Gloop can count to one hundred, but he uses all eleven of his {plural noun}, so it takes a long time. Science: Gloop planted a bean in a cup and watered it {adverb}. It grew into a {adjective} {noun}. Lunch: Gloop eats his sandwich, his apple, and sometimes his {noun}. Please pack him extra {food}.

Recess: Gloop lets the smaller monsters {verb} on his back, and he is the best at {verb ending in ing}. Last week he {past tense verb} so high on the swing that he touched a cloud.

Teacher comments: Gloop is kind, helpful, and very {adjective}. Please remind him not to hide in the {noun} during nap time.

title: A Note from the Monster Under Your Bed
text:
Dear Sam, hello! It is me, Bobo, the monster who lives under your bed. Thank you for being such a {adjective} roommate.

I have a few small requests. First, could you please stop leaving {plural noun} under here? I keep tripping on them. Second, your socks smell a little bit like {food}. I like it, but it makes my nose itchy.

Every night when you fall asleep, I fold your shirts, line up your {plural noun}, and tuck in your stuffed animals. Then I {past tense verb} around the room twice to check for crumbs. I also sing a {adjective} song to the goldfish.

On Saturday, would you like to {verb} together? I could teach you the monster dance. You wiggle your {body part}, spin around {number} times, and then flop down like a {noun}. Sleep {adverb}, Sam. If you need anything, knock on the floor three times and I will bring you a {noun}.

Your friend,
Bobo
P.S. The goldfish says thank you for the {plural noun}.

title: Help Wanted at the Fuzzy Hair Shop
text:
HELP WANTED: The Fuzzy Hair Shop needs a new helper! We are the only barbershop in town just for monsters.

Our customers are very hairy. Some have hair on their {body part}, and one has hair that is {adjective} and {number} feet long. Every haircut takes three hours, so you must be patient and {adjective}.

Your jobs will include sweeping up fur, washing {plural noun}, and handing out {plural noun} to monsters who sit still. When customers feel nervous, you will need to {verb} for them. Every day the owner, Mrs. Tangle, makes a big pot of {food} soup for lunch.

Last week a monster named Wally {past tense verb} right out of the chair because the water was too {adjective}. Now we warm the water {adverb} before every wash. If you are good at {verb ending in ing}, please come in and say hello! Bring your own {noun}.

title: Today at the Grumbly Tummy Cafe
text:
Welcome to the Grumbly Tummy Cafe, where monsters and people eat together! Our famous Monster Pancakes are as big as a {noun} and come with a side of {plural noun}. Very hungry monsters may order {number} stacks.

Today's soup is warm, {adjective}, and full of {plural noun}. It comes with a crunchy grilled {noun}. Please do not eat the bowl. We only have a few left.

For dessert, try our Wobbly Jelly Surprise! It shakes {adverb} on the plate and tastes like {food}. Some customers say it makes them want to {verb}. To drink, we have milk, apple juice, and a fizzy {color} drink called Swamp Bubbles.

Please be patient with our {adjective} waiter, Mr. Fluff. He has six arms, but he is still learning to carry plates while {verb ending in ing}. Yesterday he {past tense verb} into the dessert cart, and everyone clapped.

title: Interview with the Library Monster
text:
This week our class interviewed Mopsy, the friendly monster who lives in the school library. Mopsy is {color}, fluffy, and about as tall as a {noun}. First we asked what she does all day. "I put books back on the shelves," she said. "I also dust the {plural noun} and read stories to the {adjective} little kids."

Next we asked about her favorite food. Mopsy smiled {adverb} and said, "I love {food} with a little bit of honey on top." Then Jake asked what she does when it thunders. "I hide under the big table and try to {verb}," she said.

Our last question was about her hobbies. Mopsy likes {verb ending in ing}, knitting, and collecting {plural noun}. Last summer she {past tense verb} in a contest at the fair and won a {adjective} ribbon.

Mopsy says never use a {noun} as a bookmark. And if you return your books on time, she will give you a big, {adjective} hug.

title: How to Make Friends with a Monster
text:
So you want to make friends with a monster? Good news! Most monsters are shy, gentle, and very {adjective}. Just follow these steps.

Step one: Say hello in a soft voice. Monsters have {number} big ears, so loud noises make them {verb}. A little wave with your {body part} is also nice. Step two: Bring a snack to share. Monsters love {food}, but they also enjoy crunchy {plural noun}. Never offer a monster a bowl of soup. They will wear it as a {noun}.

Step three: Play hide and seek. Monsters are not very good at hiding. My monster friend hid behind a {noun}, and everyone could see him {verb ending in ing}.

Step four: Give the monster a compliment. You could say, "You have the most {adjective} fur I have ever seen!" Monsters love this and will blush {adverb}. Once you are friends, your monster might even {verb} with you at the bus stop. Just remember to share your {plural noun}.

title: A Monster Joins the Soccer Team
text:
Good morning, Maple Town! This is Rosie Park with the morning news. Our big story today: a monster has joined the Maple Town {plural noun} soccer team.

His name is Big Ted. He is seven feet tall, very fuzzy, and as {adjective} as a kitten. Coach Diaz says Ted is the best goalie the team has ever had. "He just stands in front of the goal," she said. "Nobody can get the ball past his {body part}."

Ted does have a few things to learn. At his first game, he picked up the ball and {past tense verb} all the way to the snack table. He also stops to {verb} whenever he sees a {noun}. After every game, he gives everyone a ride on his {adjective} shoulders and a cup of {food}. The team has won {number} games in a row.

The next game is Sunday at the park. Fans are asked to bring {plural noun} and cheer {adverb}. Ted will be the one {verb ending in ing} in the {adjective} socks.

title: Rules for Camp Snuggleclaw
text:
Welcome to Camp Snuggleclaw, the summer camp for friendly monsters! Please read the camp rules so everyone has a {adjective} time.

Rule one: Lights out is at nine o'clock. If you snore, please snore {adverb} so you do not wake your cabin buddies. Rule two: Please do not eat the canoes. We know they look like {plural noun}, but they are boats. We only have {number} canoes left.

Rule three: At campfire time, you may toast marshmallows on a stick, but please do not toast your {plural noun}. Rule four: Monsters with more than four {plural noun} must take turns on the swings. Last summer, a monster named Flurp {past tense verb} on the swings for six hours. Rule five: Wear a {color} hat on every hike.

Rule six: Write a letter home every week. Tell your family about the {adjective} {noun} you found in the woods and how you learned to {verb} like a {animal}. Have fun, be kind, and remember: at Camp Snuggleclaw, we never stop {verb ending in ing}!

title: Postcard from a Monster at the Beach
text:
Dear Mom and Dad, greetings from Sunny Sands Beach! I am having a {adjective} time. The hotel bed is too small, so I sleep on the balcony with my feet hanging over the edge. Yesterday I built a sandcastle as big as a {noun}. A seagull tried to take my sandwich, so I gave him half. Now we are best friends. His name is {name}.

Today I tried surfing for the first time. I fell off {number} times, but on my last try I {past tense verb} all the way to the shore. Everyone on the beach clapped {adverb}. A little boy asked if my fur was soft, so I let him pet my {body part}. A grandma gave me a hat because she said my ears looked {adjective}.

Tomorrow I am going to {verb} with the dolphins and eat {plural noun} for lunch. I will bring you a seashell and a {adjective} {noun}. I miss you, and I miss {verb ending in ing} in our swamp.

Love,
Snorkel
P.S. Please feed my pet {animal} while I am gone.

title: The Monster Talent Show Program
text:
